title: The same covariate name, two instruments
question: When the source and target measure a matched effect modifier with different instruments, how is the MAIC estimate biased, does a reliability correction recover it, and can a bounded analysis over declared instrument differences contain the truth?
design: Continuous-outcome MAIC with a latent modifier recorded by the source and reported by the target through linear instruments with offsets, slopes and error; 45 cells crossing instrument pairs, source reliability and modification strength; naive, reliability-corrected and bounded analyses. 1000 replicates per cell.
answer: MAIC's bias from a modifier measured by different instruments follows a closed form in the instruments' offsets, slopes and the source reliability. A reliability correction removes it only when both trials use the same instrument; with differing instruments it left bias up to 0.18 and could undo a chance cancellation. An envelope of corrected intervals over declared instrument differences covered the truth at 1.4 to 2.9 times the naive width.
findings: Naive bias on its closed form: slope 0.992 (SE 0.009) over 45 scenarios; zero without modification.
Shared instrument: reliability-corrected bias within 3 MCSE in 12 of 12 scenarios with modification.

Differing instruments: corrected bias above 0.05 in 15 of 18 scenarios, up to 0.176; at reliability 0.6 a target offset cancelled the attenuation in the naive analysis (bias -0.018) and the correction removed the cancellation (0.172).
Bounded analysis over declared instrument differences: coverage 0.967 to 1.000, width 1.36 to 2.93 times naive.
not_answered: Linear instruments and identity link only; misclassification of binary covariates and bridging-sample correction not run; target sampling error absent. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: Target-population mean difference, A versus C
methods_compared: bounded analysis over declared instrument differences
